main.headline: Voters pass data center limits as Democrats sweep midterms
main.summary: Redbud Consulting says 38 of 44 ballot measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers have passed so far, according to Ars Technica. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor race and plans to delay projects until laws on water, electricity, air and property rights pass. Bloomberg reports about 13 gigawatts of Texas data center capacity is exposed. Transformer's Shakeel Hashim argues the results raise the odds that Congress passes strong frontier AI legislation next year.

main.headline: Anthropic releases open-source FlashProve to verify which model produced an output
main.summary: Anthropic published FlashProve, a prototype that uses cryptographic proofs to show an output came from a specific model without revealing its weights. Anthropic says one H100 GPU generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second for Llama 4 Maverick, at roughly 70 to 95 times the GPU time of running the model. Code and specifications are on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. TechCrunch reports there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab.

europe_brief.headline: Aker CEO calls Microsoft's Nscale pullout a minor contract
europe_brief.summary: Aker CEO Øyvind Eriksen, whose company owns about 23% of Nscale, said Microsoft's cancelled lease was "expected" and small within a bigger portfolio. Tech.eu reports Microsoft cancelled after learning the Essex data center was unlikely to have power until after 2030, ahead of Nscale's planned IPO at a $35 billion valuation.

europe_brief.headline: UK proptech Supa raises £21 million seed round
europe_brief.summary: Supa raised £21 million in seed funding, with an equity round co-led by 2150 and OpenOcean plus a debt facility. The company buys local block management firms and applies AI to administrative tasks; it manages about 20,000 homes through seven firms.
item_titles: Supa raises £21M in seed funding to transform UK residential block management
